question: Where can I get the routes (geometry) of electricity transmission and distribution lines in the United States, with voltage level, operator and status?

answer.summary: No national government layer of US line routes is live: DHS's HIFLD Open, still cited by EIA, was withdrawn in 2025. An Esri archive (data to 2024-09-30) keeps 94,619 transmission segments (about 69 kV+) with voltage, owner and status, though many are inferred or blank. Distribution routes exist only per utility (tested: National Grid NY, 1,913 feeders). California's CEC publishes a current official layer (6,838 segments, with proposed lines). OpenStreetMap adds uneven operator/voltage tags. No national planned-lines layer was found.
main_caveats: HIFLD Open (DHS) was sunset in 2025; the usable copy is an Esri archive with data to 2024-09-30, no longer updated, while EIA's FAQ still points to HIFLD.
Counts are line segments (polyline features), not circuits or route-km; 59,111 of 94,619 HIFLD segments are flagged INFERRED=Y.
HIFLD attributes are incomplete: no OWNER 17,990, no STATUS 20,819, VOLTAGE<=0 14,248. OWNER is not a verified operator.
Distribution geometry is utility by utility; only National Grid NY (1,913 feeders) was tested.
Planned lines are not systematic: HIFLD has no planned class; CEC's 14 'Proposed' lines include stale 2014-era entries.
OpenStreetMap completeness is uneven and the public Overpass server returned 406/502 errors during tests.
answer.confidence_reason: Layers and fields were queried on 2026-11-20; the 2025 HIFLD sunset rests on secondary pages (no DHS notice opened); utility and RTO coverage beyond the examples was not checked.

key_fields.meaning: Segment identifier in the HIFLD layer.
IN SERVICE, NOT AVAILABLE, INACTIVE or UNDER CONSTRUCTION.
AC/DC and OVERHEAD/UNDERGROUND.
Owning utility name (upper case); 'NOT AVAILABLE' when unknown. This is ownership, not a verified operator.
Nominal kV as a number; zero or negative values mean unknown.
Voltage class band such as UNDER 100, 100-161, 220-287, 345, 500, 735 AND ABOVE, DC.
Y when the route was inferred rather than directly traced.
End substations of the segment.
Validation method (IMAGERY, UNVERIFIED...), validation date, source text and source date.

how_to_use.example_request: curl -G 'https://services2.arcgis.com/FiaPA4ga0iQKduv3/arcgis/rest/services/US_Electric_Power_Transmission_Lines/FeatureServer/0/query' --data-urlencode "where=VOLT_CLASS='735 AND ABOVE' AND STATUS='IN SERVICE'" --data-urlencode 'outFields=*' --data-urlencode 'resultRecordCount=2' --data-urlencode 'outSR=4326' --data-urlencode 'f=geojson'
how_to_use.example_result: 2 LineString features; e.g. ID 100170: OWNER APPALACHIAN POWER CO, VOLTAGE 765, VOLT_CLASS 735 AND ABOVE, SUB_1 CLOVERDALE 765KV, SUB_2 JACKSONS FERRY, STATUS IN SERVICE, INFERRED N, 56 vertices from (-80.823, 36.879).
steps: Query /0/query with where, outFields and outSR=4326; maxRecordCount is 2000, page with resultOffset.
Or use the item's Extract capability (shapefile, GeoPackage, GeoJSON export) from the item page.
Filter STATUS, VOLTAGE>0 and INFERRED according to the quality you need.
reading_traps: A feature is a segment, not a circuit: parallel circuits and multi-voltage lines may be split or merged.
OWNER is not necessarily the operator.
A different HIFLD copy in the GeoPlatform org (owner cherndon0, edited 2023-09-05) has only 52,244 features: vintages differ.

problems: The original DHS HIFLD Open hub could not be tested: the hub pages are a JavaScript app and DHS withdrew the portal in 2025.
Layer has no copyright or description text of its own; provenance comes from the item page.
